analysis.title: Japan Economic Flash: On Hold as Expected, But We Now Forecast the Next Hike in December
key_insights: The BOJ held its policy rate at 1.25% at the October 29-30 meeting, as widely expected, by a majority vote. Board member Hajime Takata dissented and proposed a hike to 1.50%.
GS moves its forecast for the next BOJ rate hike to December 2026 from January 2027.

The Outlook Report now says underlying inflation 'is at a level that is generally consistent with the price stability target of 2 percent.' Previously it expected underlying inflation to reach 2% between the second half of fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027. All nine board members agreed on this assessment.

Governor Ueda stressed anchoring underlying inflation at 2%. Because inflation has already reached 2%, he called a visible rise from that level undesirable and said the BOJ will respond appropriately to upside risks.

The BOJ named three upside risks to underlying inflation, the same as in September: the Middle East situation, AI-related demand and exchange rates. It added vigilance over the effect of foreign central bank rate hikes on Japan through long-term bond markets and exchange rates.

Ueda said the next hike is basically data-dependent and the BOJ will weigh the outlook and risks at every meeting, including the next one. He did not rule out a December hike and gave no message to push back on market expectations for one.

Ueda said the BOJ will check the cumulative effect of past hikes gradually, especially on corporate financing for small and micro enterprises. GS reads this as meaning the pace of hikes and the terminal rate will depend on weighing upside price risks against the lagged effect of tightening.

GS gives three reasons for the December call: (1) communication that keeps a December hike open and stresses upside price risks, (2) explicit BOJ caution about foreign central bank hikes transmitting through the yen, and (3) receding bond market concern about Japan's fiscal deterioration.

GS US economists forecast a Fed hike at the December FOMC, which comes eight business days before the BOJ's December meeting. If the BOJ held, the yen could weaken on a wider rate gap, and GS thinks the BOJ would find it hard to make a decision that causes substantial yen depreciation.
If global activity and price developments lower the probability of a December Fed hike, the BOJ could wait until January.

The 10-year JGB term premium has fallen by over 20 bps since early October. GS reads this as showing bond market worry about fiscal deficit expansion in the budget requests is smaller than it assumed.
GS had expected a December hike to be avoided because it coincides with Cabinet approval of the initial FY2027 budget and the JGB issuance plan, which could raise bond volatility.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announced a phased reduction of measures to curb fuel prices such as gasoline. Some advisors have raised corporate tax hikes as a funding source for higher defense spending. GS thinks this lowers the chance that fiscal news toward year-end only raises fiscal risk.

Beyond December, GS expects a hike to 1.75% in July 2027. This assumes accelerating CPI inflation begins to slow from spring 2027, even excluding the planned consumption tax cut from April 2027, and that the BOJ takes time to assess the cumulative effect of tighter financial conditions.

risk_factors: Upside risks to Japanese underlying inflation: the Middle East situation, AI-related demand and exchange rates.
Yen depreciation from foreign central bank rate hikes, especially the Fed.
Cumulative tightening effects on the economy, which act with a lag, especially on corporate financing for small and micro enterprises.
Bond market volatility if Japan's fiscal deterioration concerns return around the FY2027 budget and JGB issuance plan in December.
A lower probability of a December Fed hike could push the BOJ's next hike to January.

tension_points.bull_case: A December hike is likely. Ueda kept it open, cited yen depreciation risk from foreign central bank hikes, and did not push back on market expectations. The Fed is expected to hike eight business days earlier, and fiscal worries in the JGB market have eased.
tension_points.bear_case: The cumulative lagged effect of past hikes, especially on small and micro enterprises, could argue for waiting. The BOJ may also tie its timing to the Fed, so a lower chance of a December Fed hike could push the BOJ to January.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A reduced probability of a December rate hike by the Fed, which could push the BOJ's hike to January.

theme_stances.key_argument: Ueda kept a December hike open, the BOJ is cautious about yen weakness from foreign rate hikes, and bond market fiscal worries have eased.
theme_stances.evidence: We are bringing forward our forecast for the next BOJ rate hike
